🧭 **F-2665-3 — THE RT-01 CLAUSE'S `public/skill.md:367` CITATION IS ROTTED BY +4, AND ITS TRIGGER IS TOMORROW (measured and cured s2665).** The `:367` the law cites TWICE resolves today to `<!-- skillmd-guard:seeds:end -->` — a **SEEDS** fence marker — while the sentence it actually names, *"Held out means withheld from development before opening, not secret after opening, and **closed rotations remain public history**"*, now sits at **`:371`**. The rotations fence moved with it: `375–408`, where the clause quotes `371–404` (and `375–421` after the `r2026w39` mint, where it quotes `371–417`). **SUBSTANCE INTACT — the promise is unchanged, only its coordinate moved; I EYE-CHECKED `:371` by reading it back rather than trusting the re-grep.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, NOT a false green, nothing is broken, and no mint was ever wrong — `skillmd-guard` asserts the fence by PARSED CONTENT (`deepEqual`), never by line number, so the gate could not have been fooled by this.** 🎯 **What earns it a row is WHEN it fires: **RT-01 is owed TOMORROW** (`r2026w39` opens `2026-09-21T00:00:00.000Z`; F-2568-1 forbids minting on the Sunday, and today IS Sunday). F-2594-1's cure — *fill the fence with the WHOLE registry, not just the minted rotation* — rests its entire argument on that one sentence, so a minting fire that follows the stale number lands on an unrelated fence marker, finds no promise about closed rotations, and has every reason to conclude the history requirement was retired. That is the DELETE-the-history direction F-2594-1 exists to prevent, reached by obeying F-2594-1.** 🔑 **AND THE RE-BASE HAD A SECOND, SHARPER REASON THAN TIDINESS: the guard reported BOTH `:367` citations as `NEW POINTER`, and `law-pointer-guard --update` **REBUILDS THE WHOLE BASELINE** (F-2595-1). Re-basing only the live one would have let `--update` PIN A FALSE COORDINATE — a stale pointer blessed into the baseline reds nothing ever again. Both were re-based, then the baseline diff was audited entry-by-entry (F-2639-1) rather than read off the summary: `87 → 87` entries, exactly **1 removed / 1 added / 0 changed**, and the added entry carries the **IDENTICAL fingerprint `a10cd718e923`** as the removed one — which is the proof that it is the same line renumbered and not a different line blessed. Guard re-run: **PASS**, 97 pointers, 0 rotten.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: `law-pointer-guard` IS the mechanism and it worked — it named both coordinates, in its own output, unprompted. What failed is that nothing made a fire LOOK before the duty's dated trigger; the guard only speaks when a battery runs. The cure is this row plus the re-based citation at the site.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is a scheduling lesson rather than a measurement one: **a pointer into a file that a DATED DUTY is about to rewrite is the one most worth re-checking, and the worst possible moment to discover its rot is the moment the duty fires.** The fence at `375–408` grows `+13` lines EVERY WEEK by design, so every coordinate below it in `public/skill.md` is on a weekly rotting schedule that nothing else in this factory tracks. When a duty's trigger is on the calendar, re-grep its citations the fire BEFORE — not the fire OF.**

🗃️ **F-2562-2 — A BARE-DATE GIT WINDOW SLIDES WITH THE CLOCK, AND F-2391-1’S BUSY-DAY CONTROL PASSES WHILE AIMED AT THE WRONG DAY (measured s2562; amendment landed in `scripts/fire.md` §TK-01 and a comment at the site).** F-2391-1 cures the JS side of the window trap — build bounds by integer y/m/d arithmetic, never `Date` parsing — and prescribes one control: *"before trusting a zero, run the same probe over a day whose count you already know is non-zero."* **I did both and was still wrong.** 🔑 **THE MECHANISM IS IN GIT, WHICH IS WHY THAT CURE CANNOT REACH IT: approxidate fills a BARE `YYYY-MM-DD` with the CURRENT TIME-OF-DAY, so `--since=D --until=D+1` means `[D@now, D+1@now)` — the window slides through the day and the SAME command returns different days’ commits depending on what o’clock a fire runs it.** 📊 **MEASURED BY PREDICTION, 5/5, at 16:03 local: bare `--since=D --until=D+1` returned exactly the commits in `[D@16:03, D+1@16:03)` — 08-27→`0`, 08-28→`68`, 09-11→`8`, 09-12→`2`, 09-13→`29`. GROUND TRUTH, built with NO window at all by bucketing every first-parent commit on its own `%cI`: 08-27→`1`, 08-28→`0`, 09-11→`0`, 09-12→`8`, 09-13→`2`. Every bare reading names a DIFFERENT DAY.** ✅ **The offset-explicit form reproduces F-2391-1’s OWN recorded judgement to the digit (08-27 = one fire lock line, 08-28 = none) — corroboration, not a second guess.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, NOT a false green, and NO SHIPPED TOOL HAS THIS BUG — all four live users verified by READING, not inferred: `gazette-backfill-sweep.mjs`’s `normalizeSince` pins `T00:00:00` (its reason was UNDOCUMENTED until now and is a comment at the site as of this fire), `red-inventory-lookup.mjs:64` passes a full ISO `startTime`, `runner-processes.sh:31` and `start-lane-runner.sh:108` pass `@<epoch>`.** 🎯 **WHAT EARNS IT A CLAUSE IS THE DIRECTION, AND IT INVERTS F-2391-1’S: that defect returned `0` FOR EVERY DAY and failed toward doing NOTHING. This returns a PLAUSIBLE NON-ZERO COUNT FOR THE WRONG DAY and fails toward FABRICATING WORK. I read `08-28 → 68 commits, no digest` and `09-11 → 8 commits, no digest`, and was one step from compiling and committing an owner-facing ticker digest for a day with ZERO commits, and from publishing "TK-01 has two holes" as a finding. **What stopped it was recognising the 8 commits as the ones the 09-12 digest already reported — recognition, not method.**** ➡️ **CONTROL UPGRADED: build a ground truth that USES NO WINDOW and assert the windowed count equals it. A control that shares the window’s own mechanism cannot audit the window.** ⓘ **TK-01 re-measured with the corrected form and DISCHARGED: `61` digests spanning 2026-07-10 → 09-13; the single coverage day with no digest (08-27) holds one fire LOCK commit, correctly not news. The series is WHOLE.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, restraint INHERITED rather than re-argued: F-2391-1 already declined one because "did a fire hand-type a correct date window?" is unobservable to every battery (the F-1669-1 reason), and that holds identically for the sliding form.** 💡 **REUSABLE, a NEW AXIS: twenty-odd findings in this streak ask how a SUBJECT SET can be wrong — too narrow, wrong tree, wrong axis, a registry not a census, entries not files. **This one has the right subject set and a control that passes while AIMED ELSEWHERE.** F-2215-1 taught us to assert a control PRODUCED something; the rung below is to assert it produced something ABOUT THE RIGHT SUBJECT — and the only proof is a measurement taken by a method that could not have produced the same error.**

A detector never shown to hit reports a vacuous green, and this corpus has shipped that mistake five times under `gate-caller-audit`'s own name. 📊 **THE MEASUREMENT, BOTH SURFACES.** **`scripts/`** (79 `*.test.mjs`, 100+ other `*.mjs`, every `*.sh`): **27** candidate path-lists, **14** of them `tmp-`/`_s` one-shot scratch — retained evidence under the RETENTION LAW, explicitly out of scope, never swept.
